split_runtime_boundary.finding: None of the six tested inherited target face names addresses live output topology. Executable faceOf expressions alone are insufficient proof of a valid selection. These are not counted as codemod-only bugs.
split_runtime_boundary.limitation: Does not prove absence of every possible non-index reference, such as tool-derived or other structural selectors.

implementation.ownership: Runtime body bindings contain physical identity, semantic identity, root-module variable/array paths and face IDs independently of tags.
implementation.named_references: Face bindings distinguish selectedBody.sketch.tags from selectedBody.faces; rendering and body coercion use a shared resolver.
implementation.materialization: Adding a missing tag edits the defining feature, then qualifies it through a binding containing the selected face. The declaration is ensured in the actual edited AST even if runtime metadata came from a later tagged execution. Untagged imported definitions require a source-module edit and are rejected safely.
implementation.replacement: Module artifact state preserves zero/one/many replacement outputs across module teardown and cached replay. Consumed inputs are not public live bindings.
implementation.topology: Ambiguous or replaced topology is checked against engine child UUIDs before metadata advertises named references.
implementation.source_scope: AST lookup checks name availability at the edit position. Existing historical inputs remain available to legacy edit paths.
implementation.aliasing: The latest available alias supplies the physical body input. The earliest direct tag-bearing binding supplies the named tag, preserving references across merged aliases and engine/mock execution. Tag creation uses an alias containing that face, independently of whether a named tag already exists.
implementation.instance_tags: An explicit execution flag records remapped instance-local tags instead of inferring them from sketch IDs.
implementation.cache: Cached and fresh execution share the same outcome conversion.

resolution.status: Resolved with stronger engine topology checks
resolution.pattern_copy: The old assertion used original_id() as prototype identity and required Wall/Cap subtrees. Instance-local original_id now identifies the copy; topology_id retains the source. Copied PrimitiveFace records reference the semantic body artifact; independent engine checks verify their physical face ownership.
resolution.imported_patterned_composite: The old helper required duplicated Wall/Cap sweep subtrees. The graph deliberately represents copied faces with direct body ownership and source-face provenance. Tests now validate both supported representations against actual engine child UUIDs.
resolution.face_creator: A real bug remapped the support body through the retained prototype map while leaving its external support face unchanged. Cloning now preserves the external face/owner pair when the support face is not part of cloned topology. The regression checks that the face belongs to the original support body and is absent from both source and cloned output bodies.
resolution.production_change: Only CreatorFace remapping changed; pattern/composite fixes update outdated assertions and add independent geometry checks.

bounds_and_remaining_gaps: This is bounded interaction coverage, not a proof over all KCL programs or every possible selector.
Two split outputs retain inherited tag values that do not identify their live faces. Boundary tests ensure metadata excludes those stale selectors; fixing runtime inheritance remains separate.
Runtime public paths cover solids, arrays and tuples. Object-valued containers and arbitrary module namespace graphs are not included.
Coverage compares independent face/body UUIDs and engine commands, but does not drive viewport hit-testing.
Additional combinations involving multi-region sketches, holes, loft, revolve and sweep remain possible; existing individual feature regressions do not exhaust their interactions.

Source graph traversal remains for old graphs, historical edits and adding absent tags. This change does not replace the complete artifact graph or introduce primitive-index references as successful named selectors.
